summary.title: Anatomy of the .claude/ Folder
summary.one_liner: You learn what each file in the Claude Code .claude/ folder (CLAUDE.md, rules, commands, skills, agents, settings.json) does and how to set them up for a team project.
keywords: how to configure claude code for a team
how do i write a claude.md file
how to create custom slash commands in claude code
how to restrict claude code permissions
takeaways: CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session's system prompt; keep it under about 200 lines and focus on commands, architecture, and non-obvious gotchas.
Split growing instructions into .claude/rules/ files, and use YAML paths frontmatter so rules load only for matching files.
Markdown files in .claude/commands/ become slash commands, and $ARGUMENTS and !`shell` syntax let them inject input and command output.
Skills are auto-invoked, bundled workflows in subdirectories with SKILL.md; agents are subagent personas with their own tools and model settings.
Use settings.json allow and deny lists for permissions, and settings.local.json or CLAUDE.local.md for personal, gitignored overrides.
summary.summary: This newsletter article is a guide to the .claude/ folder used by Claude Code, covering both the project-level folder and the global ~/.claude/ folder. It goes file by file through CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, the rules/ folder, commands/, skills/, agents/, and settings.json, with example files for each. It ends with a step-by-step setup progression and a complete directory tree. The page also includes a sponsored Postman block at the top, which is not part of the technical content.
